detail.body:
## Overview

Add nonblocking GPU duration to existing per-iteration logging. This is the timing layer split from #52061, not another implementation of #61424's scheduler counters (dependency head `650d50d154d0f7ada81a3783b1408c8a7d0193db`) or an additional workload/export API. Related proposals: #61423, #39979, #38760.

Dependency order: **#61690 (this PR)** → #61691 (workload) → #52061 (FPM exporter), after prerequisite #61424. [Next layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61691) · [Review only this layer](https://github.com/tedzhouhk/vllm/compare/5456baf475ae86db38c701fb1c10fdc0c2ea877f...eaa98b274d6e00c897216c835bc273806e8bb48d).

These dependent fork branches retain their PR numbers/reviews and target `main`; their upstream diffs are cumulative. Use the layer-only links and merge/rebase in that order. They are not a native GitHub stack because [cross-fork stacks are unsupported](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests).

## Claims

- `--enable-logging-iteration-details` automatically collects timing when log statistics and runtime support permit it. Timing defaults off; `iteration_timing_enabled` is derived before worker initialization, not a constructor or CLI option. Unsupported logging configurations retain counts-only logs with a warning.
- Only the output worker of each DP replica owns pooled `torch.Event` pairs. Scheduler snapshots and asynchronously completed durations are joined by iteration ID in `SchedulerStats.iteration_records`. GPU-duration samples use milliseconds throughout; the later FPM exporter converts to its existing seconds-based wire format.
- The recorded `model_step_cuda` interval covers execution, sampling and speculative drafting on the recorded stream, including host-submission gaps. With PP, only the last stage's output worker is timed; this may include waiting for earlier stages. It is neither kernel-busy time, whole-pipeline/request latency, nor a sum of independent streams.
- Actual execute/sample/dummy calls stay visible in `gpu_worker.py`. A same-file guard starts scheduled iterations and cancels on error; sampling continues the interval. Conditional finish remains explicit. Dummy has its own complete-lifecycle context. MRV2 is primary; MRV1 shares the instrumentation for existing Dynamo deployments during migration.
- Normal outputs carry ready samples. Tail collection permits one outstanding RPC and checks readiness/FIFO before consuming it; active execution also reaps a previously submitted query. Future completion now uses the existing `result()` path. The poll contract distinguishes an unavailable response from an empty completed response. No timing-specific CUDA synchronization or blocking flush is added.
- Per-iteration logs no longer attach current KV-cache usage to historical records; periodic KV reporting remains. This PR does not add workload/context statistics, idle heartbeats, Prometheus instruments or a publisher.

## Validation

Head `eaa98b27`: 99 focused tests and normal hooks/mypy passed; independent review found no new issue. A known 12.5ms event stays 12.5ms through the real timer/output/collector classes. FIFO probes cover poll/model ordering, empty/sample/error replies and readiness/backpressure.

Six pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada GPU cases passed with actual MultiprocExecutor, async eager TP1/PP1 and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: MRV2 normal and MRV1/MRV2 native MTP, timing off/on. Three token-output pairs matched exactly; MTP accepted 71/81 drafts in both runners. All 112 enabled worker samples exactly matched generic `elapsed_ms`; disabled cases had no timer/records. All 112 iteration log lines omitted KV usage. This is functional validation, not throughput evidence.

Core subset command (68 passed):

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_iteration_timing.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py::test_next_step_does_not_consume_pending_output -q
```

Earlier checks are preserved below with their original SHAs; they are not current-head reruns. No new throughput or multi-GPU result is claimed by this readability change.

## Details

Support is generative CUDA models with `uni`/`mp` executors and out-of-process EngineCore. Non-CUDA, pooling, Ray/external-launcher and in-process logging retain counts only. The later workload/FPM layers require timing and reject unsupported configurations. With no active logging consumer, this layer creates no timer pool, collector or timing polls.

Collection still adds event, CPU and IPC overhead. Shutdown's bounded best-effort drain can lose tails. Prior native-MTP PP2 qualification covers MRV2 async eager only; other attempted combinations failed on the timing-off baseline. Prior DP output checks passed, but teardown needed worker force-kill. Neither broad PP2-MTP support nor graceful DP shutdown is claimed.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex. Broader polling/architecture review remains open; no review replies or resolutions are included.

<details>
<summary>Earlier qualification — original source SHAs and limitations</summary>

### Start/cancel guard refinement (`07f80ade`)

The same-file `_guard_iteration_timing` now handles starting a scheduled iteration and cancelling on error. Execute passes `new_iteration=scheduler_output`; sampling uses the same guard without restarting the interval. Actual model calls and conditional finish remain visible, preserving sampling/drafting scope. Dummy already has its distinct complete-lifecycle context and is unchanged; async-output/poll sites only drain. No extra context-manager count, CUDA events, synchronization, threads or RPCs were added. Only one existing worker test gains a zero-token case.

99 focused PR1 tests, 124 full-stack tests at `2f575597`, normal hooks/mypy and independent review passed; suite counts overlap. Fourteen exact-source before/after control-flow traces match, including zero-token `start(None)`, sampling continuation and error boundaries. The dependent patches are unchanged replays.

Six immutable-source RTX 6000 Ada cases passed on `07f80ade` with actual MultiprocExecutor, async scheduling, eager execution, TP1/PP1 and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: MRV2 normal off/on and MRV1/MRV2 native-MTP off/on. Same-runner token outputs match exactly; disabled cases create zero timers/records. Enabled normal/MTP cases delivered all 48/32 timings with exact start/finish/drain/record IDs, and all native-MTP cases accepted 71/81 draft tokens. All workers exited gracefully and the GPU was clear afterward. This is functional validation, not a new throughput, CUDA-graph or multi-GPU campaign; earlier results retain their original SHAs.

### Code-ablation follow-up (`0cbfdcb6`)

Removed one-use dummy temporaries, folded output-rank selection into timer construction, removed redundant pool/pop checks, and combined the duplicate multiprocessing dummy RPC calls. The derived internal state is now named `iteration_timing_enabled`. Net reduction: 19 production lines and 23 total lines; no new repository tests or public options. Full-step boundaries and nonblocking collection are unchanged.

The unmodified baseline passed 96 focused tests; this head passed those plus two async-output cases (98 total), normal hooks/mypy, and independent review. Six out-of-tree negative ablations produced nine expected failures in existing tests, demonstrating why cancellation, deferred finishing, shared-output isolation, async timing delivery, response readiness, and resumed-poll collection remain. Four pinned-source RTX 6000 Ada GPU cases passed with actual multiprocessing execution, MRV2 async eager, normal/native-MTP timing off/on, and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: exact paired token parity, zero disabled timers, 48/32 complete positive timing records when enabled, and native-MTP acceptance 71/81 in both arms. This is correctness validation, not a new throughput or multi-GPU qualification. The inline dummy argument reads now occur inside the interval; GPU work and event count are unchanged.

### Earlier refinement qualification (`420cd0bd`)

88 focused tests and normal pre-commit/mypy passed. Independent configuration and control-flow review found no actionable regression. Nine RTX 6000 Ada cases passed: MRV1/MRV2 normal and native-MTP timing off/on, plus real in-process counts-only fallback. Same-runner paired tokens matched; native MTP accepted 71/81 draft tokens and each enabled native-MTP run delivered all 32 timings.

Compute Lab job `5035162` used four A100-SXM4-40GB GPUs and the native wheel matching base `e96c82266`. Normal PP2 with CUDA graphs passed for MRV2 async/sync and MRV1 sync: exact timing-off baseline/candidate token parity, 48 positive timings per enabled case, and exactly one timer on last-stage rank 1. TP2 x PP2 MRV2 async also passed exact token parity and 48 positive timings, with only rank 2 (PP1/TP0) owning a timer among four workers; the baseline had none. PP2 MRV2 async native MTP passed in eager mode, including the dependent full-stack workload/FPM checks. Delayed-tail and DP2 x PP2 / EP2 checks at full-stack head `80bb05d2` are reported in #61691 and #52061.

Qualification limits: the old `10828a62` timing-off baseline failed native-MTP PP2 CUDA-graph capture (timeout), MRV1 sync (missing drafter on PP0), and MRV2 sync eager (input-count assertion). These combinations are not qualified, and no production workaround was added. The DP integration outputs passed before shutdown, but worker teardown required force-kill; graceful shutdown is not claimed. This is correctness validation, not a new serving-performance campaign. A separate CPU-only entrypoint microprobe measured about 0.8 microseconds per context-managed call, or 1.6 microseconds for execute plus sample with timing off; it is not a throughput percentage.

### Earlier test-minimality and readability validation

Test-minimality follow-up `10828a62` removes duplicate routing/layout combinations, RPC argument-forwarding checks, and a timer scanning-policy test. The consolidated worker cancellation test uses a one-pair pool and rejects an intentionally unsafe event-reuse mutant in all three execution paths. 63 focused tests and normal hooks passed. Production code and docs are unchanged from `5735cc5b`; no new GPU/performance run is claimed.

Readability-only update `44f6fa12`: extracts execute/sample/dummy timing handling into three dedicated helpers in `iteration_timing.py`. Full-step boundaries, cancellation, dummy recycling, polling, and result delivery are unchanged. 70 focused tests, normal pre-commit/mypy, and an independent 20-case before/after control-flow comparison passed. Eight RTX 6000 Ada GPU smoke cases (MRV1/MRV2 × normal/native MTP × timing off/on; eager async UniProc; `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`) passed with exact same-runner token parity and nonzero MTP acceptance. The tested production files exactly match this commit. No new overhead, CUDA-graph, or multi-GPU qualification is claimed.

### Earlier automatic-enablement validation

Earlier automatic-enablement head `67f7a554`: 171 focused tests passed across iteration logging, timer/association, observability, and existing argument utilities; normal pre-commit hooks passed. The change is limited to startup/configuration, documentation, and tests. Timing is derived in EngineCore before executor/worker initialization using the actual logging state and out-of-process capability. GPU timer, collector, executor, and model-runner algorithms are unchanged from the earlier qualification below.

Five that-head Qwen3-0.6B GPU smoke cases passed on RTX 6000 Ada with eager execution and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no-feature baseline, logging-only MRV1/MRV2, logging requested with log stats disabled, and a real InprocClient. Both logging cases produced 48 positive GPU durations and 48 actual iteration log lines; worker configuration already had timing enabled before device initialization. Baseline and disabled-log-stats cases created no timers/collectors. In-process logging kept 48 counts-only lines and a warning, without timers. Same-MRV2 output tokens matched across baseline/logging/disabled/in-process cases. FlashInfer sampler JIT was disabled for this local environment; the initial missing-toolchain attempt and a corrected logging-probe false negative are retained, not counted as passes. The prior full Compute Lab campaign is not relabeled as a new-head rerun.

### Earlier full Compute Lab qualification

Self-review fixed idle-poll handoff when a DP rank resumes with dummy-only execution, and removed redundant new timing polls from synchronous dummy steps. Active execution only reaps an existing query or receives piggybacked samples; global idle/shutdown own new polling RPCs. The regression reproduced the old dummy-handoff failure. A source-backed three-dummy probe reduced extra active queries from three to zero while delivering every record; remote DP integration cases with the PR2 workload layer also verified zero active-wave timing polls.

Compute Lab qualification used two A100-SXM4-40GB GPUs, CUDA PyTorch 2.13/cu130, immutable source directories, and the published native wheel matching upstream base `e96c82266`. Functional cases below used CUDA graphs and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B, MRV1/MRV2 × sync/async × timing off/on | All eight runs passed; each enabled run returned 48 unique positive timings. On/off output token IDs matched in every pair. |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, native MTP, MRV1/MRV2 × sync/async × timing off/on | All eight runs passed with identical on/off tokens; each generated 96 tokens. MRV1 accepted 70/81 draft tokens; MRV2 accepted 72/84. |
| Qwen3-0.6B, TP2, MRV2 async, timing off/on | Both passed. Enabled: 48 timings and exactly one timer-bearing worker out of two. Disabled: zero worker timers and zero timing records. |
| PowerMoE-3b, DP2/EP2, synchronous MRV1 and async MRV2, with the PR2 workload layer | Completed dummy/queued/idle checks with synchronization intervals 16 and 64 at PR2 head `8b0eeb84`. No lost associations or active-wave timing queries. Details in #61691. |

The previously qualified standalone PR1 head `58f1fb6a` passed 549 relevant regression tests, 22 selected client tests, and both SHM readiness/overflow cases (573 total), with zero failures/skips. One PP3 case was explicitly deselected on the two-GPU allocation; that historical head rejected timing with PP>1. Heavy gated-model client E2Es were not selected; the real public-model serving cases above are separate tests, not replacements counted as upstream E2E passes. Normal pre-commit hooks passed. Upstream PR1 lint/docs were blocked by the maintainer-authorization gate before execution; full upstream Buildkite was not triggered.

Regression suites ran at `58f1fb6a`. Earlier functional runs used `e130e014`; the final restack changed tests only and their `vllm/` Git tree is identical (`22e881b30b9c6923a2221a5c6b757dc440bd1f9c`). Raw artifacts retain their actual execution SHA.

Example focused reproduction:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS='' python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_iteration_timing.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py -q
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-logging-iteration-details
```

Controlled performance results for the previously qualified full stack `af574626` are reported in #52061 separately from these observer-instrumented correctness checks. Its timing-only arm changed paired median throughput by −0.41% (decode c1), +0.04% (decode c32), +0.03% (prefill c32), and −0.79% (mixed c64) versus final-off over three launches. This is a feature-flag comparison on that complete stack, not a standalone PR1 or that-head performance run.

+"""Associate scheduled batches with asynchronously completed worker timings."""

+from __future__ import annotations

+    from vllm.v1.executor.abstract import Executor, IterationTimingPoll
+    from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput
+
+ITERATION_TIMING_SCOPE = "model_step_cuda"
+# Retry tail collection when no later model output can carry ready timings.
+# This is a CPU wakeup/RPC cadence, not a GPU sampling or measurement interval.
+ITERATION_TIMING_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.005
+# Best-effort budget for collecting pending timings before executor teardown;
+# it does not bound total engine shutdown or guarantee frontend delivery.
+ITERATION_TIMING_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 1.0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _PendingIteration:
+    details: SchedulerIterationDetails
+    output_processed: bool = False
+
+
+class IterationMetricsCollector:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._iteration_ids = count()
+        # DP dummy steps can run ahead of the normal batch queue. Keep each
+        # association until both output processing and timing have completed.
+        self._pending: dict[int, _PendingIteration] = {}
+        self._ready: list[SchedulerIterationDetails] = []
+        self._timing_poll: IterationTimingPoll | None = None
+        self._next_timing_poll = 0.0
+
+    def begin_iteration(self, output: SchedulerOutput) -> None:
+        if output.total_num_scheduled_tokens == 0:
+            return
+        counts = output.iteration_details
+        assert counts is not None
+        iteration_id = next(self._iteration_ids)
+        output.iteration_metrics_id = iteration_id
+        self._pending[iteration_id] = _PendingIteration(
+            SchedulerIterationDetails(
+                iteration_index=iteration_id,
+                num_ctx_requests=counts.num_prefill_requests,
+                num_ctx_tokens=counts.num_prefill_tokens,
+                num_generation_requests=counts.num_decode_requests,
+                num_generation_tokens=counts.num_decode_tokens,
+                elapsed_ms=None,
+                num_encoder_inputs=counts.num_encoder_inputs,
+                num_encoder_output_tokens=counts.num_encoder_output_tokens,
+                timing_scope=ITERATION_TIMING_SCOPE,
+            )
+        )
+
+    def begin_dummy_iteration(self) -> int:
+        self._receive_ready_timing()
+        iteration_id = next(self._iteration_ids)
+        self._pending[iteration_id] = _PendingIteration(
+            SchedulerIterationDetails(
+                iteration_index=iteration_id,
+                num_ctx_requests=0,
+                num_ctx_tokens=0,
+                num_generation_requests=0,
+                num_generation_tokens=0,
+                elapsed_ms=None,
+                is_dummy=True,
+                timing_scope=ITERATION_TIMING_SCOPE,
+            ),
+            output_processed=True,
+        )
+        return iteration_id
+
+    def complete_iteration(
+        self, output: SchedulerOutput, model_output: ModelRunnerOutput
+    ) -> None:
+        self._receive_ready_timing()
+        iteration_id = output.iteration_metrics_id
+        if iteration_id is not None:
+            self._pending[iteration_id].output_processed = True
+            self._complete_if_ready(iteration_id)
+        # A real output can carry earlier dummy timings, even on a zero-token step.
+        self.complete_timing_samples(model_output.iteration_timing_samples)
+
+    def complete_timing_samples(self, samples: tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]) -> None:
+        for iteration_id, elapsed_ms in samples:
+            pending = self._pending.get(iteration_id)
+            if pending is not None:
+                pending.details.elapsed_ms = elapsed_ms
+                self._complete_if_ready(iteration_id)
+
+    def _complete_if_ready(self, iteration_id: int) -> None:
+        pending = self._pending[iteration_id]
+        if pending.output_processed and pending.details.elapsed_ms is not None:
+            self._ready.append(pending.details)
+            del self._pending[iteration_id]
+
+    def take_ready(self) -> list[SchedulerIterationDetails]:
+        ready, self._ready = self._ready, []
+        return ready
+
+    def has_pending_timing(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._pending) or self._timing_poll is not None
+
+    def _receive_ready_timing(self) -> None:
+        if self._timing_poll is not None:
+            samples = self._timing_poll()
+            if samples is None:
+                return
+            self._timing_poll = None
+            self.complete_timing_samples(samples)
+
+    def poll_timing(self, executor: Executor) -> None:
+        self._receive_ready_timing()
+        if self._timing_poll is not None:
+            return
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if not self._pending or now < self._next_timing_poll:
+            return
+        self._next_timing_poll = now + ITERATION_TIMING_POLL_INTERVAL
+        self._timing_poll = executor.start_iteration_timing_poll()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Nonblocking GPU iteration timing shared by both model runners.
+
+Intervals span model execution, sampling and speculative drafting on the
+recorded stream, including host-submission gaps. Independent work on other
+streams and EngineCore scheduling are outside this timing scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import queue
+import threading
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from copy import copy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class _PendingTiming:
+    iteration_id: int
+    start_event: Any
+    end_event: Any
+
+
+class IterationTimer:
+    """Pool timing events and collect only completed GPU intervals.
+
+    Output-copy and worker threads may drain concurrently. A contended drain
+    returns immediately instead of delaying the next model execution.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_event_pairs: int,
+        event_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if num_event_pairs <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("num_event_pairs must be positive")
+        self._event_factory = event_factory or self._make_event
+        self._event_pool: queue.SimpleQueue[tuple[Any, Any]] = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        for _ in range(num_event_pairs):
+            self._event_pool.put((self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()))
+        self._pending: deque[_PendingTiming] = deque()
+        self._active: _PendingTiming | None = None
+        self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._drain_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_event() -> torch.Event:
+        return torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def start(self, iteration_id: int | None) -> None:
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("An iteration timing interval is already active")
+        if iteration_id is None:
+            return
+        try:
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_pool.get_nowait()
+        except queue.Empty:
+            # DP dummy steps can outlive the ordinary batch-queue bound.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Iteration CUDA event pool exhausted; allocating one extra pair"
+            )
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()
+        start_event.record()
+        self._active = _PendingTiming(iteration_id, start_event, end_event)
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._active is None:
+            return
+        pending = self._active
+        self._active = None
+        pending.end_event.record()
+        with self._pending_lock:
+            self._pending.append(pending)
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        # Discard this pair instead of recycling an event still in flight.
+        self._active = None
+
+    def drain_samples(self) -> tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]:
+        """Return ready (iteration_id, elapsed_ms) pairs without synchronization."""
+        if not self._drain_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+            return ()
+        ready: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
+        try:
+            while True:
+                if not self._pending_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+                    break
+                try:
+                    pending = self._pending[0] if self._pending else None
+                finally:
+                    self._pending_lock.release()
+                if pending is None or not pending.end_event.query():
+                    break
+
+                elapsed_ms = pending.start_event.elapsed_time(pending.end_event)
+                if not self._pending_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+                    break
+                try:
+                    self._pending.popleft()
+                finally:
+                    self._pending_lock.release()
+                ready.append((pending.iteration_id, elapsed_ms))
+                self._event_pool.put((pending.start_event, pending.end_event))
+        finally:
+            self._drain_lock.release()
+        return tuple(ready)
+
+    def drain_into(self, output: Any) -> Any:
+        """Attach ready samples without mutating shared empty runner outputs.
+
+        Async handles collect their samples later in get_output().
+        """
+        if output is None or not hasattr(output, "iteration_timing_samples"):
+            return output
+        ready = self.drain_samples()
+        if not ready:
+            return output
+        output = copy(output)
+        output.iteration_timing_samples += ready
+        return output
+
+
+def make_iteration_timer(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    rank: int,
+) -> IterationTimer | None:
+    """Allocate events only when timing is enabled on the model-output rank."""
+    if not vllm_config.observability_config.iteration_timing_enabled:
+        return None
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    output_rank = parallel_config.world_size - (
+        parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        * parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size
+    )
+    if rank != output_rank:
+        return None
+    return IterationTimer(num_event_pairs=vllm_config.max_concurrent_batches + 1)
